chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad who said:
I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who came back from a journey during the month of Ramadan and had not eaten anything before midday. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should fast.'

key_terms.الزَّوَالِ: Midday (when the sun passes its zenith)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a traveler who returns home during Ramadan before midday?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the ruling for a traveler who returns home during Ramadan before midday (*Zawal*) without having eaten, obligating him to complete the fast. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it distinguishes between the status of a traveler who has already broken their fast versus one who returns before the time of breaking, emphasizing the continuity of the obligation once the traveler's exemption period effectively concludes or is deemed insufficient to warrant breaking the fast. The emphasis on *Zawal* (midday) highlights the precise temporal boundary used by scholars to determine when the traveler's specific concessions end and full fasting duties resume.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad who said,
‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> about a man who comes back from a journey during a Month of Ramazan and has not eaten anything before the midday. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should Fast’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from who has said the following: “

I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who comes home from a journey in the month of Ramadan before Zawal (declining of the sun toward the west at noontime) and has not tasted any food as yet. He (the Imam) said, ’He is required to fast.’”
